evidence.observation: Single source of truth for the three kernel v3 meta headers used on both the inbound path and outbound forwarding: x-tdai-service-id (carries the panel instance id, i.e. serviceId), x-tdai-user-key (caller identity), and x-request-id (correlation id). Because the same constants are imported by the validator and by transport-fetch, the panel can never drift between the header it validates and the header it forwards.

First stage of the trace. The middleware reads x-request-id from the inbound request and falls back to randomUUID() (line 38), stores it as ctx.var.reqId and a child logger on ctx.var.log (41-42), and echoes it back on the response header (43). The finally block maps status to log level (5xx=error, 4xx=warn, 2xx=info) and suppresses info noise for static assets and successful /health checks. Because reqId is set here before routing, every later envelope — success, validation error, or the app.onError INTERNAL envelope — can stamp the same request_id.

Composition root of the panel HTTP surface. Line 20 installs requestLogger on '*' so every request gets (or inherits) an x-request-id and a ctx.var.reqId before routing. Lines 24-37 register the /api/v1 sub-app, including registerMetaProxyRoutes(api, deps) at line 26, then mount it at API_PREFIX='/api/v1' (line 15, line 37). Lines 39-48 are the terminal error handler: any unhandled throw is logged and converted into the same 4-field control envelope {code:500, message:'INTERNAL', request_id, data:null} with HTTP 500. Lines 50-56 add the static/SPA fallback, deliberately letting /api/* and /health fall through so API responses are never swallowed by index.html.

Defines the kernel response envelope contract MetaEnvelope<T> = {code, message, request_id, data} (lines 3-8) and the single mapping used to turn an envelope code into an HTTP status (lines 11-15): 400-599 map through unchanged, code 0 maps to 200, and everything else (1xx/2xx/3xx or 6xx+, e.g. not-in-scope/unknown codes) collapses to 502. This is what makes the panel a transparent meta-proxy: business codes from the kernel survive to the client, while protocol-level oddities are reported as Bad Gateway rather than leaking a bogus status.

Panel-side envelope helpers. controlEnvelope (5-16) builds a MetaEnvelope<null> with data:null; respondEnvelope (18-20) serializes an envelope with c.json using mapHttpStatusFromEnvelopeCode(envelope.code) so the HTTP status always agrees with the body code; respondControlError (22-25) reads c.get('reqId') and stamps it into request_id, so locally generated errors still carry the same correlation id as proxied kernel responses.

The header-validation stage of the trace. It derives the action from the path suffix after '/meta/' (readAction, 24-29), requires x-tdai-service-id (MISSING_INSTANCE_ID -> 400), resolves the instance through deps.instanceRegistry.resolve (INVALID_INSTANCE -> 400 on registry code 400; other errors rethrow to the app onError handler), then requires x-tdai-user-key unless the action is exactly 'auth/verify' (MISSING_USER_KEY -> 400). On success it publishes a PanelMetaContext {instanceId, gatewayEndpoint, gatewayApiKey, userKey} into c.set('panelMeta') for the route and adapter to consume.

The route stage. It registers POST /meta/* guarded by validatePanelMetaHeaders (line 149), rejects empty action (404 UNKNOWN_META_ACTION), out-of-scope actions (501 NOT_IN_SCOPE) and non-allow-listed actions (404). It parses the JSON body defensively, assembles the MetaCallContext from c.get('panelMeta') plus c.get('reqId') (170-177), runs the pre-write duplicate check for create actions, and finally calls deps.metaKernel.invoke(action, body, ctx) (204) and returns the kernel envelope through respondEnvelope (218). Local-only branches (agent/get-default-template) still emit a synthesized code:0 envelope, so every exit path is an envelope.

The adapter stage boundary. invoke() sanitizes the body (sanitizeBody strips limit/offset for non-list actions so stray pagination params cannot leak into single-entity calls), recomputes omitUserKey for 'auth/verify' independently of the middleware (defense in depth: auth/verify must never forward a user key), converts the MetaCallContext into KernelCredentials via toKernelCredentials, and posts to the fixed kernel path `/v3/meta/${action}` through the KernelHttpPort. Note both FetchMetaKernelAdapter and FetchKernelHttpAdapter are injected as deps.metaKernel / the http port, so the route depends on ports, not on fetch.

Concrete transport adapter used in envelope mode. postEnvelope delegates to executeMetaFetch(..., 'envelope'), so a non-zero kernel business code is returned to the caller rather than thrown. When the transport itself fails it catches KernelFetchError and manufactures a well-formed MetaEnvelope with the same shape: code 504 -> 'KERNEL_TIMEOUT', 502 -> 'KERNEL_UNAVAILABLE', otherwise the error message; request_id is taken from cred.requestId and data is null. This is why downstream route code can treat transport failure and kernel failure uniformly.

The outbound hop. It normalizes the endpoint, applies a 15s default timeout via AbortController (142-143), writes the outbound headers from the shared constants at 145-151: Content-Type, x-tdai-service-id = serviceId, x-request-id = reqId (reused from the panel request id when provided, else a fresh UUID at line 135), optional Authorization: Bearer apiKey, and x-tdai-user-key only when a userKey is present. It validates the raw JSON is actually an envelope (missing/non-numeric code -> KernelFetchError 502), normalizes defaults (message 'ok', request_id falls back to reqId, data to {}), and in 'envelope' mode logs non-zero codes as errors but still returns the envelope. Timeout becomes 504, any other transport error 502.

claims.claim: A panel request enters through buildPanelApp, where the requestLogger middleware is mounted on '*' before any route, minting or inheriting x-request-id and storing it as ctx.var.reqId that later becomes the envelope request_id.

buildPanelApp only mounts the HTTP surface (request logger, /api/v1 sub-app including the meta proxy, error handler, static fallback); it holds no header-validation, adapter or envelope logic itself, keeping routing composition separate from request processing.

The meta envelope contract is MetaEnvelope<T>={code,message,request_id,data} and mapHttpStatusFromEnvelopeCode is the single code->HTTP-status rule: 400-599 pass through, 0 becomes 200, and any other code becomes 502, so kernel business codes survive to the client while unknown codes surface as Bad Gateway.

Header validation for POST /api/v1/meta/* is enforced by validatePanelMetaHeaders: x-tdai-service-id must resolve via the instance registry, x-tdai-user-key is required unless the action is exactly 'auth/verify', and failures short-circuit as 400 control envelopes built by respondControlError with data:null.

The route stage (registerMetaProxyRoutes) validates the action against the allow-list, builds a MetaCallContext from the validated panelMeta plus reqId, and always answers with an envelope: either the kernel envelope passed straight through respondEnvelope, or a locally synthesized envelope for panel-only actions such as agent/get-default-template.

The adapter hop converts MetaCallContext into KernelCredentials (toKernelCredentials) and posts /v3/meta/${action}; userKey is intentionally dropped for 'auth/verify' at both the middleware and the adapter, and limit/offset are stripped for non-list actions before forwarding.

Outbound forwarding re-emits the same header names that were validated inbound (x-tdai-service-id, x-tdai-user-key) plus x-request-id and Bearer apiKey, and transport failures are normalized back into envelope shape (504 timeout / 502 unavailable) so callers never have to handle raw fetch errors.

conclusion: A request through the TencentDB Agent Memory panel flows through four decoupled stages. (1) Header/correlation: buildPanelApp installs requestLogger on '*' (app.ts:20), which reuses or generates x-request-id and stores it as ctx.var.reqId. (2) Route + header validation: POST /api/v1/meta/* is registered at app.ts:26 and mounted under '/api/v1' (app.ts:37); validatePanelMetaHeaders resolves x-tdai-service-id to a gateway endpoint/api key via the instance registry and requires x-tdai-user-key unless the action is 'auth/verify', publishing a PanelMetaContext; failures return 400 control envelopes. The route then allow-lists the action, assembles a MetaCallContext from panelMeta + reqId, and invokes the kernel port. (3) Adapter: FetchMetaKernelAdapter sanitizes the body, re-drops userKey for auth/verify, converts the context to KernelCredentials and posts /v3/meta/${action}; FetchKernelHttpAdapter runs it in 'envelope' mode via executeMetaFetch, which forwards x-tdai-service-id/x-request-id/Bearer/x-tdai-user-key and maps transport failures to code 504/502 synthetic envelopes. (4) Response envelope: every exit path returns MetaEnvelope{code,message,request_id,data}; http/envelope.ts respondEnvelope sets the HTTP status via mapHttpStatusFromEnvelopeCode (0->200, 400-599->code, else 502), so kernel business codes pass through unchanged, and unhandled errors fall to app.onError which emits {code:500,message:'INTERNAL',request_id,data:null}. The design keeps composition (app.ts), validation (middleware), routing (proxy.ts), transport (adapters) and the envelope contract (kernel/envelope.ts) each in one place, with the shared header constants guaranteeing inbound validation and outbound forwarding cannot drift.

validation.notes: Run from the workspace root with the system Node (v24.14.0). Verification is pure JSON/structure plus line-range containment against the cited source files; no network or dependency install is involved. Because MemoryPanel has no node_modules and ships no test files (package.json declares vitest, but src contains no *.test.ts and no tests/ directory exists), the declared `npm test` / `tsc --noEmit` validation could not be executed and was replaced by this self-contained script — this limitation is recorded here as required.
